// Package goodpkg is a synthetic KNOWN-GOOD fixture for
// schemaversion_stamp_gate_test.go's TestEveryPointWriteRoutesThroughPayload.
// It stands in for internal/store/store.go's own write boundary and carries
// REAL `Upsert` calls that TRANSMIT — a fixture holding only a
// qdrant.PointStruct literal proves nothing about a boundary this gate
// defines by transmission, not by construction (see 02-02-PLAN.md's "gate
// redesign" section).
//
// Three functions mirror the three shapes real internal/store source
// carries:
//
//	(a) writer.Upsert — a direct write building the point inline, mirroring
//	    Store.Upsert itself. Receiver text "w.client".
//	(b) writer.directViaLocal — a direct write where the Memory value is
//	    first bound to a local variable and then passed to payload,
//	    proving the conformance predicate accepts a legitimate refactor of
//	    the ARGUMENT while still requiring the CALLEE identity. Receiver
//	    text "w.client".
//	(c) writer.delegatingWrapper — a delegation self-call that calls
//	    w.Upsert(ctx, m) and builds no point of its own, mirroring
//	    Store.Update/Store.Supersede. Receiver text bare "w".
//
// This file carries a .go.txt extension deliberately: it is parsed from
// source bytes by go/parser, never built by `go build`/gofmt/go vet/the
// linter, so it is not swept by any of them.
package goodpkg

import (
	"context"

	"github.com/qdrant/go-client/qdrant"
)

// Memory is a minimal stand-in for store.Memory — just enough fields for
// this fixture's payload-building shapes.
type Memory struct {
	ID string
}

// writer is a minimal stand-in for store.Store: it holds a *qdrant.Client
// and exposes an Upsert method, mirroring the real package's write boundary
// closely enough for scanQdrantCalls's method-name-only match to find it.
type writer struct {
	client *qdrant.Client
}

// payload is a minimal stand-in for store.payload: the codec every
// direct-conforming write must route through.
func payload(m Memory) map[string]any {
	return map[string]any{"id": m.ID}
}

// Upsert is the direct-conforming write itself, mirroring Store.Upsert:
// builds the point inline and calls w.client.Upsert with a Payload derived
// from payload(m). Receiver text "w.client".
func (w *writer) Upsert(ctx context.Context, m Memory) error {
	_, err := w.client.Upsert(ctx, &qdrant.UpsertPoints{
		CollectionName: "goodpkg",
		Points: []*qdrant.PointStruct{{
			Id:      qdrant.NewID(m.ID),
			Payload: qdrant.NewValueMap(payload(m)),
		}},
	})
	return err
}

// directViaLocal is the second direct-conforming write: the Memory value is
// bound to a local variable before being passed to payload, proving the
// conformance predicate inspects the CALLEE identity of payload(...), not
// the shape of its argument. Receiver text "w.client".
func (w *writer) directViaLocal(ctx context.Context, m Memory) error {
	local := m
	_, err := w.client.Upsert(ctx, &qdrant.UpsertPoints{
		CollectionName: "goodpkg",
		Points: []*qdrant.PointStruct{{
			Id:      qdrant.NewID(local.ID),
			Payload: qdrant.NewValueMap(payload(local)),
		}},
	})
	return err
}

// delegatingWrapper is the fixture analogue of Store.Update/Store.Supersede:
// a wrapper that calls w.Upsert(ctx, m) and builds no point of its own.
// Receiver text is the bare "w" — distinct from the two direct sites'
// "w.client", which is what lets the real-package gate tell a delegation
// from a direct transmission by receiver path.
func (w *writer) delegatingWrapper(ctx context.Context, m Memory) error {
	return w.Upsert(ctx, m)
}
